newsitem.title: switzerland: SOCCER-ATTACKING GAMBIT PAYS OFF FOR SWISS COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATTACKING GAMBIT PAYS OFF FOR SWISS COACH.

text.p: Switzerland's coach Rolf Fringer was rewarded for choosing a more attacking new formation when Kurbilay Turkyilmaz's late goal earned his team an important 1-0 World Cup victory over Hungary on Wednesday.
The two countries are now joint-second in group three behind Norway who dropped their first points of the qualifying campaign when they were held to a 1-1 home draw by Finland.
Norway have 10 points from their four matches, Switzerland and Hungary both have six from their four but there is still plenty to play for before the qualifiers end in October.
Turkyilmaz delighted the near-capacity crowd at the Hardturm stadium where he plays his club football for Grasshoppers by driving in a flick by defender Ramon Vega with only seven minutes remaining.
Fringer had a dreadful start to his reign as Swiss coach when the team lost 1-0 to Azerbijan last August.

After a win in Finland was followed by a home defeat against Norway, he changed the system to play with three forwards for the first time to try and take Switzerland into their second successive finals. They qualified for USA'94 after a 28-year wait since their previous appearance in 1966.

Hungary came under severe pressure for much of the game, but might have stolen a half-time lead when a shot by striker Ferenc Orosz hit the post. "We kept our discipline and our patience for 90 minutes," said Fringer. "It was most important that we didn't lose our heads. I was also pleased that in the second half we were never caught on the counter-attack."

Hungary's coach Janos Csank was disappointed that his midfield did not keep the ball better on a wet pitch. It was only Hungary's eighth defeat in 41 games against the Swiss, but six of those have come in Zurich. Hungary, who have not qualified for the final stages of a World Cup since 1986, now play at home to group leaders Norway on June 8 before hosting Switzerland in an equally important return match on August 20.
Vega, whose club form with Tottenham in England has been hit by both illness and suspension, will miss that game after collecting another yellow card.
